full_judgment:
7. The suit was contested by the defendant No. 1 by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. During the trial of the suit the defendant No. 1 died and the defendant No. 1 (Ka)-1 (Kha) being substituted and adopted the written statements filed by defendant No. 1. Their case is that the suit is not maintainable in the present from and that Tofani had 16 annas interest in schedule-1, 4 annas interest in schedule-2 and 10 annas 13 gandas-1 kara-1 kranti in schedule-3 and Mohammed Ali had 4 annas interest in schedule-2 and 5 annas 6 gondas 2 kara 2 kranti interest in schedule-3, the daughters of Mohammed Ali made oral gift of their interest in favour of defendant No. 1 in the year 1313 BS Defendant No. 1 and Phuljan were then minors when their father died and they were brought up in the house of Tofani Talukder who was related to Mohammed Ali Talukdar and Tofani Talukder being satisfied with the service of defendant No. 1 orally gifted 4 annas interest of schedule-1 property to him. The 8 annas interest of schedule-2 was in Khas possession out of the property, defendant No. 1 took lease of 4 annas and Syed Ali and Amjad Ali, sons of Tofani Talukder took bandabasta of 4 annas interest orally. In this way defendant No. 1 acquired 4 annas interest in schedule-1, 4 annas interest in schedule-2 and 3. Mohammad Ali Talukder obtained the portion of the land by way of gift from his sisters, as such, the entire interest of Mohammed Ali Talukder devolved on him. The allegations of the plaintiffs that they are in possession of the disputed property by inheritance and by purchase and they are in enjoyment of usufructs of the disputed property are false. The allegation's of transpires and inter transpires are false and collusive transactions and the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 17. He further submits that as per provision of section 103 (b) (5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 every entry in a record-of-right finally published shall be the evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect but the trial court did not consider the said provision of law and erroneously passed the impugned judgment. 

 19. On the contrary Mr Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Advocate along with Mr Abul Kalam Azad Advocate submits that the trial court rightly passed the impugned judgment. He further submits that the plaintiffs categorically stated that the suit land originally belonged to Tofani Talukder and Mohammed Ali Talukder but the CS record was wrongly prepared in the name of Syed Ali, and Amjad Ali son of Tofani Talukder and Abdul Hakim Talukder the son of Mohammad Ali Talukder and the plaintiffs are the successive heirs of Mohammad Ali Talukder and the trial court rightly found the same. He further submits that the presumption of correctness of the record-of-rights is to be rebuttable provided under section 103(b)(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 and since the plaintiffs claimed that the CS record was wrongly prepared in the name of Abdul Hakim alone excluding the name of his three sisters namely, Rokabjan the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Phuljan defendant No. 64 and Rupjan defendant No. 65. He further submits that the trial court rightly found that the plaintiffs succeed to prove that the suit land was originally belonged to Mohammed Ali Talukder. The learned Advocate referred the case of Meherjan Bibi vs Naimuddin Dhali reported in 33 DLR (HCD) 126. He also referred the case of Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin Kari reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81. 

 20. He further submits that as per provision of section 103(b) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 and section 114 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, though the entry of the records-of-right has presumptive value and when the plaintiffs claimed their right then onus shifted upon the defendants. In support of his arguments he referred the decision of the case of Pramatha Nath Chowdhury vs Kamir Mondal reported in 11 DLR (SC) 392. His next argument is that though initially no prayer for declaration of title of the suit land but ultimately through amendment before this court the plaintiff-respondents amended the pleadings and claimed declaration of title of the suit land so, no question that the suit is not maintainable without any prayer for declaration of title. He prayed for dismissal of the appeal. 

 25. He deposed that Karimjan and Alekjan relinquished their interest in favour of Syed Ali and Amjad Ali the two brothers. Karimjan died leaving 2 sons 2 daughters and said two daughters of Karimjan died without any issue. Alekjan died leaving the defendant Nos. 67-71. He deposed that his father purchased land from Fuljan and Rupjan and the defendant Nos. 60-61 by kabala dated 17th Falgoon, 1345 BS and 16th Kartick, 1349 BS. He deposed that Plaintiff by inheritance obtained 2 anna and 8 gandas share in schedule-1 and 4 anna and 16 gands in schedule-2 and 3 anna and 4 ganda in schedule-3. He deposed that subsequently they purchased 0.35 cent and Amiruddin purchased from defendant No. 6 Ayub Ali by kabala dated 29-9-1949 AD and 4th Kartick 1356 BS corres-ponding to 21-10-1949. Nuruddin purchased land from Rahim Proksha by a kabala dated 71h Falgun, 1359 BS corres-ponding to 19-2-1953. Amairuddin purchased land from Rahim Baksha by two kabalas dated 12-3-1951 and 21-5-1952 AD. 

 47. The learned Advocate of the appellants submits that preparation of CS record under section 103(b) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 has presumptive value that every entry in a record-of-rights finally published shall be the evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect. In support of his argument he cited the decision of the case of Hriday Ranjan Dey vs Niranjan Dey being dead his heirs, Probate Dey reported in 10 BLT (AD) 137 = 54 DLR (AD) 16 and the case of Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin Kari reported in 30 DLR (SC) 81 wherein the principle laid down that: "According to section 103(b)(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act every entry in a record-of-rights finally published shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect."
